item.title: Re: Is there a canon history of The Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
So, is there a list of sites and do they have specialisation?

There is, but people pay attention to/ignore them as they feel.

On a given article, might get pushback from one or two people claiming that Site 437 is only for the containment of crocodilian objects or that Site 28 is for the assessment of gas-based SCP objects. Ignore this criticism, as it is pedantry disguising itself as analysis and is fundamentally unserious.

In terms of general history, not really. There are loads of different interpretations of how it was founded, when, where, why, and by who, but none of them are any more correct than any other. In fact, there's even a canon in which there is no Foundation. Go wild.

item.title: Pataphysical Containment Site
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Site Dossier

Genre (Optional): Horror, History, Other

Elevator Pitch: A site in imaginative space, to contain pataphysical/noospherical anomalies.

Central Narrative: The site is created/constructed by linking the disembodied brains of former reality benders/anartists/ etc. to a massive computational device simulating said site. All information of the to-be-contained pataphysical/noospherical entities is given/shown to the brains so they can perceive said information and imprison the anomalies via their perception.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The consciousness of the brains are themselves contained in the site. It is not revealed how the brains got separated from their bodies, but it is specified that it was an unintended occurence and the Foundation took simply advantage.

Additional Notes: As the site is only managed by non-sapient/sentient machines, to prevent an informational containment breach, it is under heavy criticism of worried Foundation researchers. (Additionally the site itself might accidentally create new pataphysical entities for containment.)

item.title: Re: Singularity - Seeking Greenlight (1/2)
item.content:encoded:
I think overall this idea/thread is nice but I have some slight concerns.

Open
Close

What I think is great

  • The story you want to bring seems to have been thought through and definitely has some depth. You also mentioned how you plan on doing that (mostly logs and interviews) which is great. I also think the theme of guilt and your narrative compliment each other nicely.
  • I think the initial contact would make for a great discovery/addendum/…
  • You said you wanted the origin and purpose open ended which in my opinion fits the abilities and adds to the mystery of the SCP. It also makes sense since you mentioned that you plan to build more upon this in future tales and articles.

What concerns me

  • I'm interested in how you would describe/mention how the SCP clings to the researcher. It is a bit unclear to me if you will mention this quickly or rather in detail in one of the addenda.
  • The abilities that influence time in some way or form are great but I am concerned that you will overdo it. Honestly, I'm not great with these themes/things but please know that there is a difference between complex and overcomplicated. As someone who tends to do the later I recommend you type it but always check if it affects the readability afterwards.

Final verdict
I compliment you for trying the combination of a guilt/isolation theme, possible time-travel,… and I think the foundations of this idea are solid but some things need a bit fleshing out.

I think this and the concerns in this thread can all be solved by drafting in a sandbox with a good amount of commitment, time and critique. I also advise you to check the chat and draft forums for additional help should you need it. That being said, here is a second greenlight so you can use the draft forum. (I have an author page.)

Good luck with your SCP.

Hello hello Sputnik One! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

Well, as much as I believe you probably already know most of the stuff I'll say in this post, I'm sure you'll find at least one bit of helpful information - after all, you never know! Getting your first article to survive, especially as a coldpost, is quite impressive - I can't wait for what you'll write when you get critique - I'm sure it will be amazing! I can't wait to see what you come up with in the future!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings on this. On the one hand, I can totally see there being this really nice, emotional arc as the Agent trapped in the walkie-talkie like, grows as a person and learns to overcome their flaws and gradually put his old team back together and stuff; on the other, I'm not exactly sure what your plan for executing on this is?

How are you planning on telling this story? Via interview logs? Or the journal entries entirely? Why are the Foundation so willing to go along with this? It seems to me that there's some major issues with him actually doing this so like, what do the Foundation actually like, get him to do?

I kinda wonder about whether this would work as a tale: the actual narrative is extremely focussed on the SCPs growth and that usually implies to me that a story written from the perspective of the SCP would be more effective than a SCP article solely because it's easier to get into the head of the SCP that way.

item.title: Re: Utensils waiting for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I largely agree with everything caspian2 has said but I also want to add a few points of my own: namely, this really needs more narrative heft to it.

Like, you have this setup where you have the rather overcomplex anomaly but then…you have to do something with it? You have to show off why the anomaly is interesting and what the Foundation does with it and like…really try to get us invested in what is happening with the SCP, y'know?

Like, why does it matter that the Italian dude made it? What does the effects of the SCP cause to happen? What do the Foundation do with this?

At the end of the day: you're really trying to write a short story about a weird thing, not an encyclopedia entry on it, and so you kinda need to do something with this concept beyond just 'haha weird and wacky effects'.

item.title: Re: SCP-5640 The Stomach IDEA looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I think my biggest issue with this is that you don't really do a lot with the concept: while 'thing what eats people' is kinda a big trope that's been done a lot, the angle of this being used by an authoritarian government is enough of a twist that this could still work. The problem here is that the narrative around that is very passive: there's no change since all that happens is like 'the Brazilian government used it and then they fell and now they don't': this feels like it needs a like, SCP-4511 style descent where they start off putting small stuff in and then it's escalating demands forces them into more and more extreme behaviour. The downside of doing this is that as a commentary on real events, it begins to feel like it explains them as a necessary evil; and so you have to be very careful to ensure that this feels like a deliberate choice.

I think the note from the soldier encapsulates what I mean: having someone in a note plainly state "What we are doing here is heinous. A blasphemy!" is orders of magnitude less effectively in writing than showing us that it's heinous, showing us the blasphemy directly, y'know? Show us why they do it, show is why they keep doing it, show us how horrible it is.

I can appreciate the meaningful ambiguity, but at the moment, the ending entry feels a tad anti-climactic. I think that a more carefully handled progression of self-hatred might help with that.

It seems like there are multiple memetic kill agents used (scp 1 and scp 2000), so it would be odd for the foundation to let anyone with access to any scp with a kill agent to have access to scp 1. furthermore, this doesn't seem like a thing that can be deleted with amnestics, so if some researcher of an scp with a kill agent needed to edit the article in any way, they would permanently have access to 1, 2000, and every other kill agent. Maybe the kill agent articles are just incredibly incredibly exclusive, but with experimental logs, I'm not too sure about that. The only other problem I have is that it definitely seems like a big scp, and would be difficult to properly write as a second(I'm assuming second from your submissions) scp. Besides that, this is a really nice idea for how memetic kill agents work (besides the exclusivity bit). I would +1 it if you could figure out a way to circumvent the problems I said above.

item.title: Re: My SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
1) If this is negotiating with The Foundation specifically, then that means it has some sapience. This may give The Foundation a reason to try and determine if it can work out a better deal. Even if it's just basically an animal, the reason for targeting The Foundation needs to be explored.

2) Along those lines, an MTF or D-Class may be the wrong idea: The Foundation using this as a prison for its own prisoners or as a way to soften up those it interrogates may be a possibility. This would give the apartment its prisoners and give The Foundation a way to make those it arrests useful beyond any information they may otherwise offer.

Of course, there's nothing to say that the apartment could have an exclusive deal.

3) You need to emphasize the maze-like structure of the apartment. The devil's bargain works (prisoner for info/treasure) but you need to emphasize how hard it is to escape. That would create a much scarier location.

Otherwise, great idea! And your English isn't that bad.

item.title: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
I like this one, especially because of the binary option, but there are some problems:

1) I'm guessing that if you flick it off it takes your personality, if you flick it on you gain all currently absorbed personalities. This is fine, but you may want to put a limit on that if you have multiple personalities in your head only your personality is absorbed and the others are lost. Otherwise, you could potentially have a ridiculous number of personalities.

2) What are the relative strengths of the personalities? Basically, is there a struggle for control, and what kind of power do the other personalities have regarding the actions of the body? Also, are the personalities relegated to the back and can only watch or do they have any kind of voice in what happens?

3) What happens if you flick it on but it doesn't have a personality? What happens if the personality was already given to someone else? Could you absorb another personality and that personality resurrect the body, albeit under new management?

4) While I like the concept, the corpse personality drain may be one step too far. That's the only thing I would suggest dropping.

5) Strictly as a side note, the multiple personalities may actually make the Bookkeeper easier to threaten. Not only is he the receptacle of multiple lives, and thus making him more willing to make a deal; the more personalities the easier he would be to threaten. Also, the personalities may break and at least debate a deal, meaning that the weakest personality would determine if the person breaks.

But otherwise, great concept!

item.title: Cognation
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • A delve into Reality Anchor Construction and Design
  • An Thamiel anomalous SRA Component with strict rules about thinking about; the colour red, wives, or the fear of blood.
  • Additional component used in SRAs being lobotomized reality benders from Project Ichabod
  • Robert Scranton implicated to be the source of this blood.

Central Narrative: The History of the blood being used in SRAs as a Hume lowering component in addition to an advanced state of the blood with hostile telepathic properties. Going onto unravelling the source of the fluid by a researcher and going rogue sending a drone into the origin dimension. Causes a large amount of blood to be converted into the hostile counterpart. Researcher has a tell-all interview with a member of O5 revealing what and who is the source of the blood. Still image of the drone footage is shown and the blood's conversion is happening spontaneously now and will convert all amounts by 20—. O5 Command reclassifying the blood to Keter is pending.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The idea that what if Robert Scranton was the source of this SRA component, the excess humes painfully funneling into the non-dimension, changing the doctor. Turning him into a weak god in the darkness of the abyss, feeding on other gods and becoming hateful of existence itself. Basically what if the Scarlet King is a forgotten echo of a man forced to live and become a god, losing all but his attention on his wife, and waiting to break back into our reality to make existence itself suffer.

Additional Notes: Idea comes from the striking similarities of the beginning of Dust and Blood and the ending of 3001, both barely human entities stuck outside of reality, unable to die, cursed to exist only in red, with their only concern being their wives.

item.title: Brain Coral
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Conventional, with containment procedures and description followed by supplemental incident reports and experimental logs. This is followed by a "secret" file with restricted access.

Elevator Pitch: The source of all memetic kill agents used by the foundation, as well as the means of inoculation. A species of coral emits a cognitohazardous vibration that forces cardiac arrest in observers. This vibration remains hazardous in any data form. Polyps separate from the coral and enter an animal's brain, whereupon it becomes immune to the cognitohazard. All high ranking officials of the Foundation are hosting a brain parasite. This coral has formed a symbiotic relationship with the entire foundation. This means YOU have the parasite if you've ever survived the SCP-001 kill agent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The unique effects of the cognitohazard vibration are discovered when security workers are killed viewing the waveform of security footage. Research into its properties and the extent of this effect is undergone. At some point, the idea to use it for security was proposed by the heads of research, Dr. Berryman and Langford, and publicly denied. Shortly after, an "incident" on-site causes the "death" of all coral bushes. In reality, they are quietly moved to an unknown location to implement the memetic security agent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: My idea is that the true nature of the SCP is hinted at throughout the text before being revealed at the end. The Neutralized classification and description of its supposed destruction should hopefully be somewhat intriguing.

Additional Notes: No idea if this conflicts with any previous articles. As this is my first work and it attempts to retcon something so iconic it may be controversial.

The idea is that the coral will only infect animals that choose not to feed on it, and releases a vibration pulse that travels far underwater and kills all others. This poses the question of what benefit the coral would receive from not simply killing everything around it. Maybe by "whitelisting" certain animals, it can manipulate its ecosystem to evolve beneficially.

Also not sure how the parasite would get in your brain. It would need to enter in a way as to not cause long-term damage if any at all.

SCP-3000 has proven that the Foundation will utilize anomalies to their benefit, although that is arguably less extreme.

This SCP refers collectively to an entire species of coral. Each colony possesses a unique cognitohazardous vibration which can only be prevented by hosting of a polyp from the corresponding colony.

item.content:encoded:
a mysterious benevolent entity/company is trying to help humanity regain contact with their dead loved ones

I'm admittedly still skeptical about this, since not only does the entity focus on grandmas only for seemingly no reason, the requirement of antique radios doesn't feel conducive to helping humanity as a whole. Would make more narrative sense if, say, you had some anomalous tinkerer who missed his grandma messing with his own radio, which made anomalous broadcasts, which trigger manifestations in other such radios within a certain radius.

+ show block
– hide block

I still like to point out that some articles do have a similar setup as mine, which I took the inspiration from.

Those articles are not your article. Readers voting on your eventual draft are not obligated to look at other successful articles and upvote your work because those articles you did not write are successful. If they don't like your work, they'll downvote, regardless of whether something else has been similar and successful.

Also, I planned this as an initial setup for future articles of mine.

Again, focus on the piece at hand here. If the major plot point of your material is too heavily reliant on future articles, readers might feel like something is missing and the piece comes off more as sloppy rather than mysterious. Remember to keep in mind the readers' point of view—they don't automatically know what's being developed the way you as the author do. If they feel like something is missing, their immediate response is "something is missing" and not "the author must be working on something amazing that hasn't been posted yet".

Yep.

I'm admittedly having trouble believing this, but if you're certain that the audience won't be skeptical, by all means continue.

Oh yeah, that's the right word I am looking for. A tale in a format of what you've said, my bad.

A supplement page is inherently not a tale; it's an offshoot/support page for an SCP article.
